subject: Compare all combinations of a factor

messages.author: 57c14964df92e5e4
messages.subject: Compare all combinations of a factor
parts:
Hi unmarked friends,

I have run an occuRN model with two covariates, one a covariate on abundance, island vs mainland (2 levels), and the other a covariate on detection, camera type (4 levels).

The model output compares some combinations of each factor, but not all. For example, the two levels of the factor 'ki.mainalnd' are compared (highlighted in yellow), but only some comparisons are shown for the factor 'camera' (which has four levels); specifically camera 1 compared to each of cameras 2, 3, and 4 (highlighted in green). How do I obtain all the possible comparisons between each of the four levels of camera? For example, how would I obtain the comparison of camera 2 to camera 3? If anyone is able to point me in the direction of the command/commands I should be using it would be very much appreciated.

I have included some example code below.

Thanks in advance,

Pat   

> # prep data
> y <- dat[,1:8]
> siteCovs <- dat[,c("ki.mainland","site","camera")]
> obsCovs <- list(lure.age=dat[,12:19])
> final <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=y,siteCovs=siteCovs,obsCovs=obsCovs)

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Compare all combinations of a factor
parts:
Hi Pat,

If you add -1 to each component of the formula you'll remove the intercepts and obtain a "means" instead of an "effects" parameterization. Right now your level 1 of each factor is represented by the intercept, and the other coefficients represent the estimated differences between those levels and the intercept. Removing the intercept gives you the mean estimates for each factor level.

messages.author: 57c14964df92e5e4
messages.subject: Re: Compare all combinations of a factor
parts:
Hi Dan,

Thanks for this little trick. However, this is not exactly what I was meaning. The model output above allows me to determine if the detection of camera 2, 3, or 4 was significantly different to that of camera 1. When using your little trick (below) my interpretation is that I essentially obtain untransformed estimates of detection for each level of camera, i.e. the estimate value for each camera level is essentially the detection estimate but on the logit scale. What I am wanting to do is to determine if the detection of camera 2 is significantly different to that of camera 3 and 4, and if the detection of camera 3 is significantly different to that of camera 4. I am wanting the pairwise comparisons for camera. I realize that you can determine this in a roundabout way by using the confidence intervals that are produce from the below model output, but it would be nice to be able obtain the p-values for each pairwise comparision. Are you able to help with this? Does my question make sense? Please correct me if my interpretation of the model results so far are incorrect. Thanks in advance.    


> m4 <- occuRN(~camera-1 ~ki.mainland-1, final)
> m4

Call:
occuRN(formula = ~camera - 1 ~ ki.mainland - 1, data = final)
